findings.reason: a node must either extend the disposition and the check's signature, which §5's "claim_disposition is unchanged" forbids, or invent where the base and the stopped-state enter; the plan should name that plumbing and the caller that supplies it.
findings.text: §5 puts the exception in `_raise_repository_scope_conflict`, which receives a `TaskNode` with no base field (reckon/crew/node.py:737-758) and a list of `_RepositoryScopeClaim` carrying only `binding` and a free-text `disposition_reason` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:127-150), yet the exception keys on "the dispatch's base is the holder's chain tip" and "its holder is stopped"; `claim_disposition` returns `binding=True` for both a running holder (`"is still running as pid N"`) and a stopped holder holding work (`"has stopped but its worktree still holds …"`, reckon/crew/node.py:1554-1566), so neither fact is readable at that site

findings.reason: the third clause of the done-when is unbuildable from the plan, so a node either invents a site for the promotion result or silently fails the measure it was given.
findings.text: §5's done-when requires "promoting the holder while its descendant is live succeeds and its result names the live descendant", but §5's Change names no site for that result: its stated mechanisms are the scope-conflict exception, the stacking recorded on both pointers through `_mutate_pointer`, and the `_live_scope_claims` registry row (reckon/crew/runs.py:902), and no promotion or discard result reads that row

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — every symbol §5 cites resolves: `claim_disposition` (reckon/crew/node.py:1500), `_raise_repository_scope_conflict` (reckon/crew/dispatch_claims.py:1567), `_revision_is_ancestor` (reckon/crew/promotion_scope.py:2389), `_is_ancestor` (reckon/crew/merge.py:538), `_live_scope_claims` (reckon/crew/runs.py:902), and the pointer writer `_mutate_pointer` (reckon/crew/runs.py:328).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §5's done-when is measurable and names a negative control: a dispatch based on main is still refused `ScopeConflict` and the base commit fails the same test; its unbuildable promotion clause is reported under reasoning.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §5 names no gate log of its own; the landing record this plan uses (`docs/evidence/archive/a-coordinator-can-clear-its-own-duties-landed.html`) exists and is durable.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5's proposed vocabulary (stacked run, chain tip, admitted stacking) names mechanism, carrying no plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the exception is placed at a site that can read neither the dispatch's base nor the holder's stopped state, and the done-when's promotion clause names no mechanism.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §5 has one goal (a run built on a held chain tip may write its holder's paths), with the scopes-view row and the promotion/discard results as consequences of that one change.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §5 declares no depends-on/informs/gates of its own and the plan-level after-target `work-is-checked-against-its-domain#s2` resolves (docs/plans/work-is-checked-against-its-domain.html).
